chunks: And it is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said:

I read the letter of Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'Convey to my Shia that my visitation is equivalent before Allah, the Exalted, to one thousand Hajj.' I said to Abu Ja'far (meaning his son, peace be upon him), 'One thousand Hajj?' He replied, 'Yes, by Allah, and one thousand thousand Hajj for the one who visits him knowing his right.'

key_terms.بِحَقِّهِ: His right (referring to the spiritual status and rights of the Imam)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (specifically of the Imams or Prophet)
key_terms.عَارِفاً: Knowing/Gnostic (one who possesses deep spiritual knowledge)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting an Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bazanti from Imam al-Rida (a.s.), this hadith underscores the preeminence of Ziyarah in Shia piety, equating a single visit to the Imam with a thousand Hajj pilgrimages. The narration further elevates the reward to one million for those who visit with 'Ma'ifah' (gnosis of the Imam's right), highlighting that spiritual insight, rather than mere physical presence, is the key to maximizing devotional merit. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam as the living proof of God, making his visitation a central pillar of religious identity and spiritual purification.
